title: A fraction cannot be more than one whole
statement: A fraction is always part of one whole, so the numerator can never be bigger than the denominator and a fraction can never be greater than 1.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: add two proper fractions whose sum exceeds one
evidence_patterns.signature: adjusts the result so it stays below or equal to one

evidence_patterns.item_shape: place an improper fraction on a number line
evidence_patterns.signature: places it below 1 or says it cannot be placed

example.item: Mark 5/4 on a number line from 0 to 2

discriminators.vs_slip: Ask directly whether 7/4 is a number. A slip is an arithmetic error; the belief is the stated rule 'the top can't be bigger than the bottom'.

vs.math.frac.mixed-to-improper-add-all: That bug accepts improper fractions but converts to them wrongly; this belief rejects them.

conflicts_with.label: CCSS 4.NF.B.3: understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b

resolved_by.label: CCSS 4.NF.B.3: understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b
CCSS 3.NF.A.2: understand a fraction as a number on the number line

sources.citation: Stafylidou, S., & Vosniadou, S. (2004). The development of students' understanding of the numerical value of fractions. Learning and Instruction, 14(5), 503-518.
sources.note: A developmental stage in which fractions are understood as always smaller than the unit.
